players.product: High-capacity nearline HDDs (UltraSMR / EPMR / HAMR) for AI capacity-tier storage

quarterly_data.signal: LTA pricing, CEO: 'the LTAs obviously have a base price associated to a base volume', and upside delivered to customers is 'subject to a different pricing construct'. 'Quite a significant amount' of the cloud business is under LTA; because not every LTA starts and ends at the same time, WD 'will see price adjustments from LTAs even as we go through the fiscal year', depending on when contracts kick in with new pricing, which is dictated by new platforms; more rapid price increases have come in the non-nearline space. Asked whether contracted pricing is accelerating, the CEO said 'You're probably over-extrapolating a bit too much'. CEO: quarter-to-quarter gross-margin variations come from the timing of 'when existing LTAs expire and new LTAs kick in with different pricing regimes' and from next-generation platforms. CFO: 'I have high conviction that we will continue to improve gross margins for many quarters going forward'.

Exabyte ramp and customers, CEO: as WD ramps 40 terabyte shipments in the second half of the year, 'that will be over 50% of the nearline exabytes we ship, we expect exabyte growth rate to accelerate', with 44 terabyte HAMR following. Since the last update, 'additional hyperscale and cloud customers' are 'advancing through qualification and deployment planning'. 'The vast majority of the nearline bits that we're shipping are going to hyperscale customers'; WD engineering teams are working with enterprise OEMs to adopt UltraSMR and next-generation ePMR or HAMR products. WD is 'engaging with many large enterprise customers who are in the physical AI space' and sees physical AI as 'a driver of growth 2027 and beyond'; high-bandwidth drives, sampling with five customers, are seen as 'a future driver of growth'.
quarterly_data.figure: 40TB ePMR over 50% of nearline exabytes shipped in the second half; exabyte growth expected to accelerate
